local_articles.title: Marc Marquez cruises to historic sprint victory from pole at German Grand Prix
local_articles.snippet: July 11 - Marc Marquez completed a dominant Saturday at Sachsenring by following a lap-record pole position with victory in the German Grand Prix sprint race, fending off younger brother Alex Marquez to secure a record 19th MotoGP sprint win. The factory Ducati rider led throughout the 15-lap sprint race and crossed the line 0.368 seconds clear of Gresini Racing's Alex Marquez, who remained within striking distance but was unable to challenge for the lead. The result allowed seven-time MotoGP champion Marc Marquez to cut the gap to championship leader Jorge Martin to 32 points. A 12-time winner at Sachsenring across all classes, Marc Marquez continued his remarkable record at the German circuit as he bounced back from a frustrating outing at Assen last month. local_articles.title: Marquez snatches German MotoGP pole with new lap record, Bezzecchi crashes again
local_articles.snippet: July 11 - Marc Marquez broke the lap record at Sachsenring to take pole for the German Grand Prix on Saturday, clocking one minute 19.041 on his factory Ducati for his third pole of the MotoGP season. Trackhouse Aprilia's Raul Fernandez briefly held provisional pole before VR46 Ducati's Fabio Di Giannantonio, the previous circuit record-holder, moved to the top of the timesheets in the closing stages. But Marquez had the final say, producing a pair of rapid laps to reclaim top spot at a circuit where he has enjoyed unparalleled success. The Spaniard finished 0.061 seconds clear of younger brother Alex Marquez, who secured second place for Gresini Racing to complete a Marquez one-two on the grid. questions.title: Which U.S. state will be the first to impose a statewide moratorium on construction of large new hyperscale data centres?
questions.background: Hyperscale data centres are large facilities designed to provide computing and storage capacity at massive scale. Their development can place substantial demands on electricity grids and water supplies.
questions.resolution_criteria: Qualifying Event : Resolve to the first U.S. state to formally impose, by December 31, 2026, a statewide temporary moratorium on construction or permitting of large new hyperscale data centres. Proposed legislation, vetoed measures, and restrictions limited to individual municipalities do not qualify. Source of Truth : Official state-government announcements, corroborated by reliable contemporaneous news reporting. Resolution occurs when the qualifying moratorium is publicly announced as imposed. Accepted Answer Format : The name of the state.

Progressive NY primary victories and early-July heatwave power-conservation alerts further raise election-year pressure on Hochul ahead of November, while no competing state passed a statewide construction moratorium through July 6 (VA/FL/IL July 1 measures were tax/tariff/incentive policies; MN and MI actions remain municipal only; Maine's bill was already vetoed with override failed).
